---
title: "iblatlas"
---

`iblatlas` is a Python package from the International Brain Laboratory for working with the
mouse brain in the Allen Common Coordinate Framework: converting coordinates, navigating brain
regions, and plotting results on slices and flat maps.

With your own data, you can:

- **Place coordinates and probe insertions in atlas space** —
  [work with probe insertions](how-to/work-with-probe-insertions.qmd),
  [plot points on slices](how-to/plot-points-on-slices.ipynb).
- **Look up brain regions and remap between Allen, Beryl and Cosmos** —
  [remap region ids](how-to/remap-region-ids.ipynb).
- **Plot per-region values** on [slices](how-to/plot-values-on-slices.ipynb), the
  [cortical flat map](how-to/plot-on-cortical-flatmap.ipynb) or the
  [Swanson flat map](how-to/plot-on-swanson-flatmap.ipynb).

Gene expression, MERFISH cell types, lipids, mesoscale connectivity and cortical depth have
already been registered to the same space, so they join to your data by a coordinate or an Allen
region id, and the same plotting tools work on them. See
[external data in the common space](explanation/external-data-in-the-common-space.qmd).

## Getting started

1. **[Install iblatlas](how-to/install.qmd)** — including configuring ONE, and the first-use
   download of several gigabytes.
2. **[Work through the tutorial](tutorials/working-with-the-atlas.ipynb)** — a tour of the atlas
   object.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two conventions to know

Coordinates are in metres, relative to bregma, and depth is negative — see
[coordinates and volumes](explanation/coordinates-and-volumes.qmd).

The Needles and MRI Toronto scalings of the Allen atlas differ by about 7% in depth — see
[choosing an atlas](explanation/choosing-an-atlas.qmd).
:::
